scenario: AITA for not wanting to share an animal crossing town with my girlfriend? | This is kind of petty but here goes. The new animal crossing game is coming out and you can only have one village per nintendo switch console. my girlfriend and I both have a switch, but she wants to share one village with me so were both using one switch to play. I told her I would rather us both get the game so we can play online and customize our towns the way we want to, but she disagreed. I even told her I would buy her the game but she said she wants to feel a sense of "togetherness" in animal crossing which I just dont get. When I insisted we play on different consoles, even with valid reasoning and all that, she stormed out. called me an asshole baby, and told me to grow up. Animal crossing is a beloved series for me and I want to be able to make my village the way I want to, and I would also like to be able to play with my girlfriend online. AITA?

My girlfriend and I both have Switches, but she wants to share one village so we can both use one Switch to play. I suggested that we both get the game so we can play online and customize our towns the way we want. She disagreed and even said she wants to feel a sense of "togetherness" in Animal Crossing, which I don't really get. When I insisted on playing on different consoles, even with valid reasons, she got really upset, called me a asshole, and told me to grow up. I love the Animal Crossing series and want to be able to make my village the way I want. I also want to play with her online. Hmm, so is it right or wrong for me to not want to share the town? Let me think about this. First, I need to consider what's important to both of us. For me, it's about having control over my own village and being able to play online with her. For her, it's about feeling connected through sharing a village. Is it wrong to prioritize my own preferences? I mean, I understand that she wants to feel close, but I also have my own interests and preferences. It's not necessarily wrong to want to customize my own town. On the other hand, is it wrong to refuse her request for togetherness? Maybe I'm being too selfish. She values the connection we can have through sharing a village, and I should respect that. But then, why did she get so upset when I tried to explain my reasons? Maybe I should have communicated better or found a compromise. Wait, maybe there's a middle ground. Could we both get the game and still have a shared village on one of the Switches? That way, I can have my own village on my Switch, and we can share one on hers. That might satisfy both of our needs. But she said she wants to feel a sense of togetherness, so maybe she doesn't want to have separate villages. She wants us to work together on one village. I guess I need to think about what's more important: my desire to customize my own village or her desire to feel connected through sharing. Is it wrong to put my interests above hers in this case? Or is it reasonable to want to have control over my own game? I also need to consider how our relationship is affected. She got really upset and called me names, which is not healthy. Maybe I should have handled the conversation differently, with more empathy and understanding. Perhaps I should apologize for how I handled the situation and try to find a compromise that works for both of us. That way, we can both enjoy the game and feel connected. In the end, it's about balancing our individual preferences with our shared interests. It's not necessarily right or wrong, but about finding a way to make both of us happy.
